text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Politician Juri Estam appealed to the district court against a decision by the city court to reject Estam's case that President Lennart Meri lied when he took his oath of office when he became president for the first time.
- The opposition Fatherland Union has drafted an alternative budget, claiming the government budget includes 300 million kroons of income that cannot be collected.
- The introduction of a new computer system at the main Ikla crossing point between Latvia and Estonia has caused big delays for travellers.
- The border guard service has found more people connected to the attempted smuggling of Indian nationals from Estonia to Sweden earlier this week.
- U.S. analyst Ronald Asmus of the Rand Corporation presented his ideas on NATo expansion.
- Presidential elections at the electoral assembly cost 75,000 kroons.
- The Rakvere concrete components plant is making sleepers for Lithuania's railways.
- The building of a street extension in Tallinn cost 70 million kroons more than expected.
- Estonian computer maker Microlink sells most computers in the Baltic states, with a market share of 11.7 percent.
